# Device files and model detection

- Global allowlists are `_SYR_CONNECT_<PLATFORM>_SUPPORTED_KEYS` in the read-only platform modules (`sensor.py`, `binary_sensor.py`, `update.py`). They are built from the entity descriptions (`_SYR_CONNECT_<PLATFORM>_TYPES`). The platforms that write to the device (select, switch, button, valve) have no global allowlist: only the allowlists of a device file enable them, and a model without a device file has none of them. A model may override the global allowlists per platform in a device file `devices/<name>.py` with `SENSOR_SUPPORTED_KEYS`, `SELECT_SUPPORTED_KEYS`, `SWITCH_SUPPORTED_KEYS`, `BINARY_SENSOR_SUPPORTED_KEYS`, `BUTTON_SUPPORTED_KEYS` and `VALVE_SUPPORTED_KEYS`. An override replaces the global set completely.
- Every device file collects its allowlists in `PROFILE = SyrConnectDeviceProfile(...)` (`devices/__init__.py`). `_SYR_CONNECT_MODEL_PROFILES` in `models.py` maps the model name to it (`"<model>": <name>.PROFILE`); without a profile a model uses the global allowlists. An allowlist of `None` keeps the global allowlist of the platform, for a device without a fixture.
- Use positive allowlists only. Do not add exclusion lists to the models (`models.MODELS`) or their signatures.
- An override must still contain structurally required keys such as `dst`, otherwise `registry_cleanup()` deletes them.
- An empty override (`set()`) is valid and means "no entities". Always check `is None` when reading an override.
- A key in a device file needs an entity description of its platform (`_SYR_CONNECT_<PLATFORM>_TYPES`). For the read-only platforms it is then also in the global allowlist, except for the sensors in `_SYR_CONNECT_SENSOR_PROFILE_ONLY_KEYS`. Selects, switches, buttons and valves are enabled by a device file alone, and so are computed sensors of one family (`getCND_class`, SafeTech water hardness range).
- The official per-model validity matrix in `docs/syrconnect-protocol.md` beats fixture contents. A key that is present in a fixture can still be a stub value. Only judge by fixture for properties the matrix does not cover.
- Fixture co-presence of a key across models does not prove it is generic. When domain knowledge and fixture data conflict, ask the maintainer.
- A model has two parts with the same name: its signature in `aiosyrconnect/model_detection.py` (`dk`/`dkv`/`sbt`/`dfm`, status checks, local path `base_path`, alarm commands, alarm, notification and warning codes, name, manufacturer and branding, limits of its settings) and its device profile in `_SYR_CONNECT_MODEL_PROFILES` of `models.py` (`None` without a profile). A new model needs both. `models.MODELS` combines them in the order of the signatures of the library, which decides the status checks; `tests/test_models.py` checks that both lists match. `models.UNKNOWN_MODEL` is `UNKNOWN_MODEL_SIGNATURE` of the library without a profile.
- Match the exact `dk`/`dkv` in `aiosyrconnect/model_detection.py` before mapping a name from the matrix to a device file. Similar names can be different products.
- Device file names use underscores (valid module names) and describe the role, for example `muco_filling`. Do not use the raw `getDFM` number, its meaning differs per `dk`/`dkv` family.
- `detect_model_signature()` of the library (called by `models.detect_model()`) first selects the signatures with the cloud `dk`/`dkv` (and `sbt`, if the signature sets it). One signature is the result; in a larger family the status checks decide between its signatures only. The status checks over all signatures are the fallback for the local JSON API and unknown device kinds. Keep `dk`/`dkv` of every signature correct, and give each signature of a family a status check that tells it apart. Do not add generic catch-all signatures for a family, an unknown role must stay an unknown model. The MultiController roles (`getDFM`) come from the dkv table in `docs/syrconnect-protocol.md`.
- `dfm` is the MultiController role (`getDFM`), the subtype of dk 1500-1506. Like `sbt`, it narrows the signatures before the family and the status checks; a signature without `dfm` matches every device.
- Rebrand siblings share one device file (for example all NeoSoft rebrands). A change affects the whole family, grep `<name>.PROFILE` in `models.py` first.
- Device modules are imported statically in `models.py`. Add new files there, do not use `importlib` at runtime. `tests/test_device_files.py` checks that every device file is referenced by a signature.
- When renaming a device file, search the whole repository for the old name. Docstrings and test names reference it as plain strings.
- There are no generic alarm, notification or warning codes: every device family numbers them differently. The code tables live in the library (`aiosyrconnect/codes.py`), and every signature names the tables of its family (`ala_codes`, `not_codes`, `wrn_codes`). A family with its own alarm codes has a table `ALA_CODES_<family>`. NeoSoft, Trio, SafeTech+ (dk 1112) and the MultiController share `ALA_CODES_COMMON`, `NOT_CODES_COMMON` and `WRN_CODES_COMMON`. Families that expose getNOT/getWRN without known codes use `NOT_CODES_NONE`/`WRN_CODES_NONE`, which only map "no notification"/"no warning". A table maps the code to the key of its meaning, which is the state key of the sensor in `translations/*.json`. A model without codes shows the raw code.
